    57	 *   This function will be called to dynamically set aside the heap region.
    58	 *
    59	 *   - For the normal "flat" build, this function returns the size of the
    60	 *     single heap.
    61	 *   - For the protected build (CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED=y) with both kernel-
    62	 *     and user-space heaps (CONFIG_MM_KERNEL_HEAP=y), this function
    63	 *     provides the size of the unprotected, user-space heap.
    64	 *   - For the kernel build (CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL=y), this function provides
    65	 *     the size of the protected, kernel-space heap.
    66	 *
    67	 *   If a protected kernel-space heap is provided, the kernel heap must be
    68	 *   allocated by an analogous up_allocate_kheap(). A custom version of this
    69	 *   file is needed if memory protection of the kernel heap is required.
    70	 *

    72	 *
    73	 *     .data region.  Size determined at link time.
    74	 *     .bss  region  Size determined at link time.

    76	 *     Heap.  Extends to the end of SRAM.

    79	 *

    81	 *     Kernel .bss  region  Size determined at link time.

    84	 *     Padding for alignment

    86	 *     User .bss region  Size determined at link time.

    88	 *     User heap.  Extends to the end of SRAM.
    89	 *

   265	   * same size.  If that is not true for this particular device, then
   266	   * transform the start block and nblocks as necessary.
   267	   */

   269	  /* Read the specified bytes into the provided user buffer and return
   270	   * status (The positive, number of bytes actually read or a negated
   271	   * errno)
   272	   */

   274	    {
   275	      return -EINVAL;
   276	    }
   277	  nxmutex_lock(&g_lock);

   279	  ret = bk_flash_read_bytes(offset, buffer, nbytes);
   280	  if (ret == OK)

   300	static ssize_t beken_write(FAR struct mtd_dev_s *dev, off_t offset,

   331	  int ret = -EINVAL; /* Assume good command with bad parameters */

   372	              info->sectorsize  = MTD_BLK_SIZE;

   376	            }

   383	           * taken into account of calculating hash value, so it is not

   396	        }

   399	      case MTDIOC_ERASESTATE:

   404	          ret = OK;
   405	        }
   406	        break;

   432	  uint32_t blocks = mtd_size/MTD_BLK_SIZE;

   435	  if (!mtd_part)

   437	    return NULL;
   438	  }
   439	
   440	  return mtd_part;
   441	}

   443	/****************************************************************************
   444	 * Name: beken_mtd_init
   445	 *
   446	 * Description:
   447	 *   Create and initialize an MTD device instance.  MTD devices are not
   448	 *   registered in the file system, but are created as instances that can
   449	 *   be bound to other functions (such as a block or character driver front
   450	 *   end).
   451	 *
   452	 ****************************************************************************/
   453	
   454	FAR struct mtd_dev_s *beken_mtd_init(void)
   455	{
   456	  /* Allocate an instance of the private data structure -- OR, if there can
   457	   * only be a single instance of the driver, then use a shared, global
   458	   * device structure.

   460	  if (!g_mtddev.initialized)

   463	        {
   464	          return NULL;
   465	        }
   466	      g_mtddev.initialized = true;
   467	    }
   468	
   469	  /* Return the implementation-specific state structure as the MTD device */
   470	
   471	  return (FAR struct mtd_dev_s *)&g_mtddev;
   472	}

   100	/****************************************************************************
   101	 * Name: up_idlepm
   102	 *
   103	 * Description:
   104	 *   Perform IDLE state power management.
   105	 *
   106	 * Input Parameters:

   108	 *
   109	 * Returned Value:
   110	 *   NULL.
   111	 *
   112	 ****************************************************************************/
   113	
   114	static void up_idlepm(void)
   115	{
   116	  static enum pm_state_e oldstate = PM_NORMAL;
   117	  enum pm_state_e newstate;
   118	  irqstate_t flags;
   119	  int ret;
   120	
   121	  /* Decide, which power saving level can be obtained */
   122	
   123	  newstate = pm_checkstate(PM_IDLE_DOMAIN);
   124	
   125	  /* Check for state changes */
   126	
   127	  if (newstate != oldstate)
   128	    {
   129	      flags = enter_critical_section();
   130	
   131	      /* Perform board-specific, state-dependent logic here */
   132	
   133	      _info("newstate= %d oldstate=%d\n", newstate, oldstate);
   134	
   135	      /* Then force the global state change */
   136	
   137	      ret = pm_changestate(PM_IDLE_DOMAIN, newstate);
   138	      if (ret < 0)
   139	        {
   140	          /* The new state change failed, revert to the preceding state */
   141	
   142	          pm_changestate(PM_IDLE_DOMAIN, oldstate);
   143	        }
   144	      else
   145	        {
   146	          /* Save the new state */
   147	
   148	          oldstate = newstate;
   149	        }
   150	
   151	      /* MCU-specific power management logic */
   152	
   153	      leave_critical_section(flags);
   154	
   155	      switch (newstate)
   156	        {
   157	        case PM_NORMAL:
   158	          sleep_mode = PM_MODE_DEFAULT;
   159	          break;
   160	
   161	        case PM_IDLE:
   162	          sleep_mode = PM_MODE_NORMAL_SLEEP;
   163	          break;
   164	
   165	        case PM_STANDBY:
   166	          _info("Device will enter the standby mode\n");

   168	          bk_gpio_register_wakeup_source(GPIO_12,GPIO_INT_TYPE_FALLING_EDGE);

   179	          bk_gpio_register_wakeup_source(GPIO_18,GPIO_INT_TYPE_FALLING_EDGE);
   180	          bk_pm_wakeup_source_set(PM_WAKEUP_SOURCE_INT_GPIO, NULL);
   181	          sleep_mode = PM_MODE_LOW_VOLTAGE;
   182	
   183	          bk_pm_sleep_mode_set(PM_MODE_LOW_VOLTAGE);
   184	          bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_APP,0x1,0x0);
   185	          bk_pm_suppress_ticks_and_sleep(0);

    54	/****************************************************************************
    55	 * Name: beken_aes_cbc_cypher
    56	 *
    57	 * Description:
    58	 *   Process AES CBC encryption/decryption.
    59	 *
    60	 * Input Parameters:
    61	 *   ctx     - AES context
    62	 *   encrypt - True: encryption mode; False: decryption mode
    63	 *   ivptr   - Initialization vector pointer
    64	 *   input   - Input data pointer
    65	 *   output  - Output buffer pointer
    66	 *   size    - Data size in bytes
    67	 *
    68	 * Returned Value:
    69	 *   OK is returned on success. Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned.
    70	 *
    71	 ****************************************************************************/
    72	
    73	int beken_aes_cbc_cypher(arm_ce_sca_context_t *ctx, bool encrypt, void *ivptr,
    74	                         const void *input, void *output, uint32_t size)
    75	{
    76	  int ret;
    77	
    78	  DEBUGASSERT(ctx && input && output && ivptr);
    79	  DEBUGASSERT(size && ((size % AES_BLK_SIZE) == 0));
    80	
    81	  ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_aes_lock);
    82	  if (ret < 0)
    83	    {
    84	      return ret;
    85	    }
    86	
    87	  ret = arm_ce_sca_crypt( ctx,
    88	                          ( encrypt ?
    89	                            ARM_CE_SCA_OPERATION_ENCRYPT :
    90	                            ARM_CE_SCA_OPERATION_DECRYPT ),
    91	                            ARM_CE_AES_CBC,
    92	                            0,
    93	                            size,
    94	                            NULL,
    95	                            ivptr,
    96	                            NULL,
    97	                            input,
    98	                            output );
    99	  if (ret < 0)
   100	    {
   101	      return ret;
   102	    }
   103	
   104	  ret = nxmutex_unlock(&g_aes_lock);
   105	  if (ret < 0)
   106	    {
   107	      return ret;
   108	    }
   109	
   110	  return OK;
   111	}

   233	/****************************************************************************
   234	 * Name: aes_cypher
   235	 *
   236	 * Description:
   237	 *   Process AES encryption/decryption.
   238	 *
   239	 * Input Parameters:
   240	 *   out     - Output buffer pointer
   241	 *   in      - Input data pointer
   242	 *   size    - Data size in bytes
   243	 *   iv      - Initialization vector pointer
   244	 *   key     - Key data pointer
   245	 *   keysize - Key data size in byte
   246	 *   mode    - encryption mode, AES_MODE_CBC or AES_MODE_CTR
   247	 *   encrypt - True: encryption mode; False: decryption mode
   248	 *
   249	 * Returned Value:
   250	 *   OK is returned on success. Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned.
   251	 *
   252	 ****************************************************************************/
   253	
   254	#ifdef CONFIG_CRYPTO_AES
   255	
   256	int aes_cypher(void *out, const void *in, size_t size,
   257	               const void *iv, const void *key, size_t keysize,
   258	               int mode, int encrypt)
   259	{
   260	  int ret;
   261	  uint8_t iv_buf[AES_BLK_SIZE];
   262	  uint8_t cache_buf[AES_BLK_SIZE];
   263	  size_t nc_off;
   264	  static arm_ce_sca_context_t ctx;
   265	
   266	  if ((size & (AES_BLK_SIZE - 1)) != 0)
   267	    {
   268	      return -EINVAL;
   269	    }
   270	  if ((keysize != 16) && (keysize != 24) && (keysize != 32))
   271	    {
   272	      return -EINVAL;
   273	    }
   274	
   275	  if ((mode != AES_MODE_CBC) &&
   276	      (mode != AES_MODE_CTR))
   277	    {
   278	      return -EINVAL;
   279	    }
   280	
   281	  ret = beken_aes_init(&ctx);
   282	  if (ret < 0)
   283	    {
   284	      return ret;
   285	    }
   286	
   287	  ret = beken_aes_setkey(&ctx, key, keysize * 8);
   288	  if (ret < 0)
   289	    {
   290	      return ret;
   291	    }
   292	  switch (mode)
   293	    {
   294	      case AES_MODE_CBC:
   295	        memcpy(iv_buf, iv, AES_BLK_SIZE);
   296	        ret = beken_aes_cbc_cypher(&ctx, encrypt, iv_buf, in, out, size);
   297	        break;
   298	      case AES_MODE_CTR:
   299	        nc_off = 0;
   300	        memcpy(iv_buf, iv, AES_BLK_SIZE);
   301	        ret = beken_aes_ctr_cypher(&ctx, &nc_off, iv_buf, cache_buf,
   302	                                   in, out, size);
   303	        break;
   304	      default :
   305	        ret = -EINVAL;
   306	        break;
   307	    }
   308	  return ret;
   309	}

   311	#endif

    82	/****************************************************************************
    83	 * Name: beken_rng_read
    84	 ****************************************************************************/
    85	static ssize_t beken_rng_read(struct file *filep, char *buffer,
    86	                              size_t buflen)
    87	{
    88	  struct rng_dev_s *priv = (struct rng_dev_s *)&g_rngdev;
    89	  ssize_t read_len;
    90	  uint8_t *rd_buf = (uint8_t *)buffer;
    91	
    92	  if (nxmutex_lock(&priv->rd_lock) != OK)
    93	    {
    94	      return -EBUSY;
    95	    }
    96	
    97	  read_len = buflen;
    98	
    99	  /* Wait until the buffer is filled */
   100	
   101	  while (buflen > 0)
   102	    {
   103	      uint32_t word = (uint32_t)bk_rand();
   104	      uint32_t to_copy = MIN(sizeof(word), buflen);
   105	
   106	      memcpy(rd_buf, &word, to_copy);
   107	      rd_buf += to_copy;
   108	      buflen -= to_copy;
   109	    }
   110	
   111	  /* Release rd_lock for next read */
   112	
   113	  nxmutex_unlock(&priv->rd_lock);
   114	  return read_len;
   115	}

   622	/**
   623	 * @brief Register a pre-sleep callback with execution priority
   624	 *
   625	 * This callback will be called BEFORE the system enters sleep mode.
   626	 * Callbacks are executed in priority order (0=first, 255=last).
   627	 *
   628	 * Typical use cases:
   629	 *   - Save peripheral states
   630	 *   - Power down devices
   631	 *   - Flush buffers
   632	 *
   633	 * @param callback  Function to call before sleep (must not be NULL)
   634	 * @param arg       User argument passed to callback (can be NULL)
   635	 * @param priority  Execution priority: 0 (highest) to 255 (lowest)
   636	 *                  Use predefined constants: PM_CALLBACK_PRIORITY_*
   637	 *
   638	 * @return  0  Success
   639	 *         -1  Invalid callback (NULL pointer)
   640	 *         -2  Out of memory
   641	 *
   642	 * Memory cost: 16 bytes per registration (32-bit ARM, aligned)
   643	 * Time complexity: O(n) insertion, O(n) execution
   644	 *
   645	 * Example:
   646	 *   void uart_pre_sleep(void *arg) {
   647	 *       // Save UART state and power down
   648	 *   }
   649	 *   bk_pm_pre_sleep_callback_register(uart_pre_sleep, NULL, PM_CALLBACK_PRIORITY_HIGH);
   650	 *
   651	 * Priority table example:
   652	 *   Priority 0   (CRITICAL): Clock manager, PMU
   653	 *   Priority 50  (HIGH):     UART, SPI
   654	 *   Priority 100 (NORMAL):   GPIO, ADC
   655	 *   Priority 150 (LOW):      Sensors
   656	 *   Priority 200 (LOWEST):   Debug logging
   657	 */
   658	bk_err_t bk_pm_pre_sleep_callback_register(sleep_callback_t callback, void *arg, uint8_t priority);
   659	
   660	/**
   661	 * @brief Unregister a pre-sleep callback
   662	 *
   663	 * @param callback  Function to remove
   664	 *
   665	 * @return  0  Success
   666	 *         -1  Invalid callback (NULL pointer)
   667	 *         -2  Callback not found
   668	 *
   669	 * Memory: Frees 12 bytes
   670	 * Time complexity: O(n) where n is number of registered callbacks
   671	 *
   672	 * Example:
   673	 *   bk_pm_pre_sleep_callback_unregister(uart_pre_sleep);
   674	 */
   675	bk_err_t bk_pm_pre_sleep_callback_unregister(sleep_callback_t callback);
   676	
   677	/**
   678	 * @brief Execute all pre-sleep callbacks
   679	 *
   680	 * This function is called automatically by the PM system before entering sleep.
   681	 * Application modules should NOT call this directly.
   682	 *
   683	 * Execution order: LIFO (Last-In-First-Out)
   684	 * - The most recently registered callback executes first
   685	 *
   686	 * Time complexity: O(n)
   687	 */
   688	bk_err_t bk_pm_pre_sleep_callback_execute(void);

   695	 *

   713	 * Example:

   222	
   223	static int gpio_read(struct gpio_dev_s *dev, bool *value)

   225	  struct beken_gpio_dev_s *beken_io_dev = (struct beken_gpio_dev_s *)dev;

   234	    }

   300	static int gpio_attach(struct gpio_dev_s *dev,

   309	    {
   310	      /* Make sure the interrupt is disabled */
   311	      BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_disable_interrupt(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   312	      BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_register_isr(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id, beken_gpio_int_wrapper));
   313	
   314	      gpio_devs[beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.virtual_gpio_id].callback = callback;
   315	    }

   326	 * Name: gpio_enable
   327	 *
   328	 * Description:
   329	 *   Enable or disable the interrupt of GPIO.
   330	 *

   333	 *   enable       - The flag of enable or disable interrupt.
   334	 *

   336	 *   OK           : The function execute successfuly.

   342	static int gpio_enable(struct gpio_dev_s *dev, bool enable)

   345	
   346	  if (beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio.gp_pintype >= GPIO_INTERRUPT_PIN )

   357	      else

   360	          BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_disable_interrupt(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   361	        }
   362	    }
   363	  else
   364	    {
   365	      gpioerr( "ERROR: The gp_pintype %d is not be supported.\n", beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio.gp_pintype);
   366	      return -EACCES;
   367	    }

   372	/****************************************************************************
   373	 * Name: gpio_setpintype
   374	 *
   375	 * Description:
   376	 *   According to the pintype to config the GPIO.
   377	 *
   378	 * Input Parameters:
   379	 *   dev          - The struct of GPIO device.
   380	 *   pintype      - Pintype to be configured.
   381	 *
   382	 * Returned Value:
   383	 *   OK           : The function execute successfuly.
   384	 *   ERROR        : The pintype is invalid.
   385	 *   Other value  : Some function execute failed.
   386	 *
   387	 ****************************************************************************/
   388	
   389	static int gpio_setpintype(struct gpio_dev_s *dev,
   390	                            enum gpio_pintype_e pintype)
   391	{
   392	  struct beken_gpio_dev_s *beken_io_dev = (struct beken_gpio_dev_s *)dev;
   393	
   394	  DEBUGASSERT(beken_io_dev != NULL);
   395	
   396	  beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio.gp_pintype = pintype;
   397	  BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(gpio_dev_unmap(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   398	
   399	  switch (pintype)
   400	  {
   401	  case GPIO_INPUT_PIN:
   402	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_enable_input(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   403	    break;
   404	  case GPIO_INPUT_PIN_PULLUP:
   405	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_enable_input(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   406	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_pull_up(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   407	    break;
   408	  case GPIO_INPUT_PIN_PULLDOWN:
   409	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_enable_input(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   410	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_pull_down(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   411	    break;
   412	  case GPIO_OUTPUT_PIN:
   413	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_enable_output(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   414	    break;
   415	  case GPIO_OUTPUT_PIN_OPENDRAIN:
   416	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_enable_output(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   417	    break;
   418	  case GPIO_INTERRUPT_HIGH_PIN:
   419	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(beken_set_input_int_type(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id, GPIO_INT_TYPE_HIGH_LEVEL));
   420	    break;
   421	  case GPIO_INTERRUPT_LOW_PIN:
   422	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(beken_set_input_int_type(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id, GPIO_INT_TYPE_LOW_LEVEL));
   423	    break;
   424	   case GPIO_INTERRUPT_RISING_PIN:
   425	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(beken_set_input_int_type(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id, GPIO_INT_TYPE_RISING_EDGE));
   426	    break;
   427	   case GPIO_INTERRUPT_FALLING_PIN:
   428	    BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(beken_set_input_int_type(beken_io_dev->beken_gpio.gpio_id, GPIO_INT_TYPE_FALLING_EDGE));
   429	    break;
   430	  default:
   431	    return ERROR;
   432	    break;
   433	  }
   434	
   435	  return OK;
   436	}

   438	/****************************************************************************
   439	 * Public Functions
   440	 ****************************************************************************/
   441	
   442	/****************************************************************************
   443	 * Name: beken_gpio_init
   444	 *
   445	 * Description:
   446	 *   Register the gpio.
   447	 *
   448	 * Input Parameters:
   449	 *   NONE.
   450	 *
   451	 * Returned Value:
   452	 *   OK           : The function execute successfuly.
   453	 *   Other value  : Failed to initial or register gpio.
   454	 *
   455	 ****************************************************************************/
   456	
   457	int beken_gpio_init(void)
   458	{
   459	  int rtn_value;
   460	
   461	  for (uint32_t io_number = 0; io_number < (sizeof(gpio_devs)/sizeof(gpio_devs[0])); io_number++)
   462	    {
   463	      BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(gpio_dev_unmap(
   464	        gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio_id));
   465	      gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.virtual_gpio_id = io_number;
   466	
   467	      BK_RETURN_ON_ERR(bk_gpio_set_config(gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio_id,&(gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio_config)));
   468	      rtn_value = gpio_pin_register(&gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio, gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio_id);
   469	
   470	      if (rtn_value != OK)
   471	        {
   472	          gpioerr("Failed to register gpio %d  \n",gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio_id);
   473	          return rtn_value;
   474	        }
   475	
   476	      gpioinfo("Succeed to register gpio %d \n",gpio_devs[io_number].beken_gpio.gpio_id);
   477	    }
   478	
   479	  return OK;
   480	}

    43	static inline void bk_psram_byte_write(unsigned char *addr, unsigned char value)
    44	{
    45		uint32_t addr_align = (uint32_t)addr;
    46		uint32_t temp = 0;
    47		uint8_t index = 0;
    48	
    49		index = (addr_align & 0x3);
    50		addr_align &= 0xFFFFFFFC;
    51		temp = *((volatile uint32_t *)addr_align);
    52		switch (index)
    53		{
    54			case 0:
    55				temp &= ~(0xFF);
    56				temp |= value;
    57				break;
    58			case 1:
    59				temp &= ~(0xFF << 8);
    60				temp |= (value << 8);
    61				break;
    62			case 2:
    63				temp &= ~(0xFF << 16);
    64				temp |= (value << 16);
    65				break;
    66			case 3:
    67				temp &= ~(0xFF << 24);
    68				temp |= (value << 24);
    69			default:
    70				break;
    71		}
    72	
    73		*((volatile uint32_t *)addr_align) = temp;
    74	}

   160	{
   161		unsigned int *dst = (unsigned int*)dst_t, *src = (unsigned int*)src_t;
   162		int index = (unsigned int)dst & 0x03;
   163		int count = length >> 2, tail = length & 0x3;
   164		unsigned int tmp = 0;
   165		unsigned char *p, *pp = (unsigned char *)src;
   166	
   167		if (!index)
   168		{
   169			while (count--)
   170			{
   171				*dst++ = pp[0] | pp[1] << 8 | pp[2] << 16 | pp[3] << 24;
   172				pp += 4;
   173			}
   174	
   175			if (tail)
   176			{
   177				tmp = *dst;
   178				p = (unsigned char *)&tmp;
   179	
   180				while(tail--)
   181				{
   182					*p++ = *pp++;

   185			}
   186		}

   188		{
   189			unsigned int *pre_dst = (unsigned int*)((unsigned int)dst & 0xFFFFFFFC);
   190			unsigned int pre_count = 4 - index;
   191			tmp = *pre_dst;
   192			p = (unsigned char *)&tmp + index;
   193	
   194			if (pre_count > length) {
   195				pre_count = length;
   196			}
   197	
   198			while (pre_count--)
   199			{
   200				*p++ = *pp++;
   201				length--;
   202			}
   203	
   204			*pre_dst = tmp;
   205	
   206			if (length <= 0)

   209			}

   212			count = length >> 2;
   213			tail = length & 0x3;
